text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi, feted with a hero's welcome in Albania, said a multinational security force could aid the country's "rebirth" after weeks of armed anarchy. Prodi said Italy wants to help Albania to reconstruct the state and to have quick, democratic transparent elections. More than 10,000 cheering Albanians greeted Prodi in the rebel-held southern port city of Vlore, birthplace of a violent uprising that has claimed nearly 300 lives (all).

* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini joined a demonstration organised by centre-right opposition and said moderate political forces ought to reach a broad agreement in order to create a political alternative that did not include hard-left Communist Refondation (all).

* Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said concerning the reform of welfare state it would be possible to discuss retirement age which could be calculated on the basis of actual working years (all).

* Trade unions' representatives will meet Prodi, treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and labour minister Tiziano Treu to discuss government programme of incentives to the labour market, unions blame majority coalition for not keeping its promises (La Stampa).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
